provenanceNote: Carries no referenceDate on purpose, which makes this two assertions in one. Denmark's century comes from a published table rather than an inference, so no reference date is needed to parse. And a ten-digit number has no long form, so Short has no century to elide and equals Display -- where Sweden's Short would fail with ReferenceDateRequired, Denmark's renders.

The single most important Danish case. Born 2016, so issued well after CPR stopped applying modulus-11 in 2007, and it does not satisfy modulus-11. CPR states such numbers are fully valid -- 'Personnumre uden modulus 11 er fuldt ud gyldige personnumre' -- so a parser enforcing modulus-11 rejects this real person. Do not add a modulus-11 check and do not delete this fixture when someone proposes one.

Serials run 0001-9999, so DDMMYY-0000 is not a CPR number and no bearer can exist. It is rejected by the century table rather than by a separate range check: a serial of 0000 falls outside every row, so the lookup has nowhere to resolve it. The reported failure changed in spec 0.3.0 and Denmark's behaviour did not. Six digits, a hyphen and four digits is also a shape-valid Finnish personal identity code, so once Finland became recognize-only the most specific answer available stopped being 'no scheme recognised this shape' -- the precedence table ranks unsupported-scheme above not-an-identity-number precisely because a recognition is more informative than the fallback. Denmark's refusal is still pinned here by outcome: failed, which would go red if the century table ever accepted a serial of 0000. The unhyphenated companion fixture pins the original failure code with no foreign shape in play.

30 February exists in no century, so no bearer can exist. The serial is 3001 rather than the 3000 a person would reach for first, because that form is Luhn-valid as a Swedish ten-digit short form and the provenance gate flags it. Writing the rejected value out here would trip the gate too, which is why it is described rather than quoted.
Serial 5000 with year 32 resolves to 2032, after the reference date. Safe to construct precisely because no bearer can exist yet: CPR has not issued numbers to people not yet born.

The same non-number written without its separator, which Finland's shape cannot match because the seventh character has to be an intermediate character and here it is a digit. Added when Finland became recognize-only, so the plain 'Denmark refuses a serial of 0000 and no other scheme has an opinion' assertion survives somewhere in the corpus. Serials run 0001-9999, so no bearer can exist.
